p3.title: Clinical Synthesis & Key Findings
p3.sub: Non-SOAP format. Prepared from the supplied PosturePulse assessment and supplemental metric summaries.
p3.reviewed: 21/21 video-derived posture metrics; supplemental posture and bilateral thermal summaries
p3.synthesis: The supplied PosturePulse AI capture (scan_id 9339f15b, 19 Nov 2026) reports angular, linear offset, and thermal symmetry metrics for technical review rather than clinical diagnosis. Several frontal tilt measures—including head lateral tilt, shoulder-line tilt, hip-line tilt, trunk lateral lean, and bilateral knee extension—have uncertainty intervals that overlap the 0-degree reference, meaning no definite deviation can be inferred from those values. Small non-overlapping intervals appear in lateral body shift (-2.2 to -0.2% stature) and bilateral trunk inclination (-2.9 +/- 2.4 deg left; -4.0 +/- 2.3 deg right), alongside unreferenced regional review points and side-to-side offset differences. These are supplied measurements, not a diagnosis, and any clinical decisions require symptoms, physical examination, and standardized repeat measurement.

findings.label: Regional review points (R1-R4)
findings.text: Head/ear (80.7 deg), shoulders (87.4 deg), pelvis (87.0 deg), and trunk (85.5 deg) are flagged against a 90 deg comparator as system-selected review points rather than universal cutoffs. Missing direction, side, or anatomical plane metadata, along with differing definitions, prevent attributing these values to a definite deviation.

findings.label: Comparator and thermal points (G1, G2-G3, REF)
findings.text: Left/right knee values (1.9 / 2.2 deg) fall within the supplied 0-5 deg comparison band, and trapezius/lumbar temperatures (+0.0 / +0.0 C) show bilateral thermal symmetry at capture, which does not represent a clinical clearance. The blue reference chain represents landmark orientation points only without diagnostic classification.

findings.label: Frontal tilt and lean proxies (Table A)
findings.text: Head lateral tilt (-0.7 +/- 8.9 deg), shoulder-line tilt (-0.6 +/- 3.5 deg), hip-line tilt (-0.6 +/- 7.0 deg), and trunk lateral lean (-0.8 +/- 1.8 deg) all have uncertainty intervals overlapping the 0 deg reference, so no definite deviation can be inferred. Knee frontal alignment (+4.9 / +1.3 deg) has no reference set and wide uncertainty, preventing diagnostic classification.

findings.label: Lateral body shift (Table A)
findings.text: Lateral body shift is -1.2 +/- 1.0% stature, giving a stated interval of -2.2 to -0.2% stature that does not overlap the 0% stature reference. This reflects a small negative geometric translation in the supplied capture.

findings.label: Sagittal offsets from ankle (Table B)
findings.text: Ear (+5.0 +/- 1.5% L vs +2.6 +/- 1.5% R), hip (+4.2 +/- 1.5% L vs +0.7 +/- 1.5% R), and knee (+1.8 +/- 1.5% L vs +0.1 +/- 1.6% R) offsets show side differences without a supplied source reference. Shoulder offset shows opposite signs (+2.6 +/- 1.5% L vs -1.7 +/- 1.5% R), requiring verification of stance and camera calibration before attribution.

findings.label: Head-shoulder, trunk inclination, and knee extension (Table B)
findings.text: Knee extension (+0.8 +/- 5.1 deg L; +1.4 +/- 5.1 deg R) has uncertainty intervals overlapping 0 deg on both sides, so no definite deviation can be inferred, and the 6.5-deg side difference in proxy head-shoulder angle (+80.1 +/- 5.5 deg L vs +73.6 +/- 5.5 deg R) is smaller than the combined uncertainty. Bilateral trunk inclination (-2.9 +/- 2.4 deg L; -4.0 +/- 2.3 deg R) remains below the 0-deg reference across both stated intervals.

p3.integrity: Keep each measurement layer separate and do not average across regional review angles, frontal proxy tilts, sagittal offsets, or thermal readings, as definitions, planes, and comparators differ. Note also the record metadata discrepancy between patient ('Priya') and source_record ('Priyw'), and account for missing plane or side labels on R2 and R3.
p3.qualification: These numbers cannot establish any diagnosis, structural disorder, pathology, or clinical clearance. Where uncertainty intervals overlap 0 deg or lack a source reference, no definite deviation or clinically meaningful asymmetry can be inferred from the figures alone.

p5.title: Clinical Implications & Management Framework
p5.sub: Translates the measured pattern into a safe clinical workflow. Not a diagnosis or treatment prescription.
p5.significance: Most angular tilt and knee extension metrics have wide uncertainty intervals that overlap the 0-degree reference, meaning no definite deviation is demonstrated for those measures. A few metrics—specifically lateral body shift and bilateral trunk inclination—show small intervals outside 0, while side-to-side sagittal offsets lack source references and may reflect stance or calibration factors. Overall, the pattern is a mix of overlapping intervals, unreferenced asymmetries, and small geometric translations that require context before interpretation.

steps.rule: Record pain, aggravating tasks, neurologic symptoms, work exposure, tolerance and prior injury.
Assess relaxed stance/gait, regional motion, landmarks, strength, sensation, reflexes and relevant provocation.
Match camera setup, stance, clothing, lighting and software; obtain at least two trials.
If symptomatic, use position changes, ergonomic adjustment and graded mobility/strength work.
Prompt assessment for progressive deficit, gait change, bowel/bladder or saddle symptoms, severe night pain, fever, trauma or systemic illness.

p5.outcomes: A repeat measurement should verify consistent stance, landmark placement, and camera calibration, particularly for the opposite-sign shoulder offset and unreferenced sagittal differences. It should evaluate whether the small non-overlapping intervals in lateral body shift and trunk inclination persist across standardized captures.
p5.limitations: This single capture cannot assess symptoms, functional movement, repeatability over time, or the true anatomical planes where metadata were omitted. Proxy landmark angles and unvalidated comparison bands do not reflect underlying clinical status.
p5.evidence: Single-session optical or landmark-based posture measurements are sensitive to subject stance, camera calibration, and landmarking variance, as reflected in the wide +/- 1.8 to +/- 8.9 deg uncertainty intervals. Because these values are unvalidated against clinical outcomes, measurement noise can obscure or mimic small geometric differences.
p5.conclusion: This technical summary does not support a diagnosis, structural label, or clinical clearance. Values whose uncertainty intervals overlap the reference permit no definite inference of deviation, and any clinical decisions require symptoms, physical examination, and standardized repeat measurement.
